description.purpose: The import adapter for foreign history (ADR 0012): it decomposes ONE write batch - a whole transcript handed out as a single message - into single-turn episodes in the order of the day, fires each at the memory hive's EXISTING write lane, and keeps its own ledger so that the same batch delivered twice writes nothing the second time. Built as the missing piece between a closed session and the central memory (GH #101); that gap closed the other way, because since GH #298 (ruling Q11) the conversation speaks one turn per message and nothing shipped wires this hive any more. What is left is bulk import: a haystack, an exported transcript, an archive month. It lives outside the memory hive and speaks only its documented lanes: not one line of the hive changes.
description.use_when: For an out-of-band bulk import of foreign history, and for nothing else (ADR 0012; GH #298, ruling Q11): a benchmark haystack, an exported transcript, an archive month - wherever a batch really is a batch and a repeated delivery must be a skip. Nothing in this distribution wires it. NOT on a live conversational path: a talky's `turn_write` route hands out ONE turn per message, already in the shape the memory hive's in_episode lane reads, so a decomposer in front of it is a second minter over turns that lane already wrote. To use it, instantiate it and wire all three ports in the SAME mutation (see PORTS below). The edge that carries the batch IN owes it the provenance the memory requires: context.audience_set and context.channel.
description.not_in_scope: Neither the fact path nor the episode path of a LIVE conversation passes through here any more (ADR 0012, GH #298 ruling Q11): both are written per turn, straight at the hive's in_episode lane. Not the transfer lane either (#243): that moves a hive's OWN records and re-derives nothing; this derives episodes from foreign raw conversation. No extraction, no summarising, no judgement about what is worth remembering - append-all. No LLM call and no provider key: the write path is model-free by spec. No second write path into memory. No session lifecycle. No recall lane - this adapter only writes. And no provenance of its own: it carries the participant set and the room through, it never mints them and never defaults them to `["*"]`.
examples: PORTS - Entry: in_batch, wired as {from: <talky>, to: <drain>, condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'write', modifier: {set_hop: {route: 'in_batch'}, set_context: {session_id: 'hop.session_id'}}}. Exit: 'episode' -> the memory hive's in_episode lane, wired as {from: <drain>, to: <memory>, condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'episode', modifier: {set_hop: {route: 'in_episode'}, set_context: {session_id: 'hop.session_id', turn_id: 'hop.turn_id', happened_at: 'hop.happened_at'}}}. Exit: 'reject' -> wherever refusals are read, wired as {from: <drain>, to: <sink>, condition: has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'reject'} - required, and the mutation refuses the in_batch edge without it.

a 6-turn day closes -> 6 episodes with turn_ids s1#0 .. s1#5 land in the hive's episodes table, one per turn, in the order of the day, each carrying the participant set and the room the batch arrived with
the same day is closed a second time (or the batch is replayed) -> the ledger says 6 of 6 -> NOTHING is written, the row count does not move
the session grew to 8 turns since the last drain -> only s1#6 and s1#7 are written

a day arrives over an edge that carries no context.audience_set -> nothing is parked, nothing is marked, one message leaves on 'reject' with hop.reject_reason 'missing_audience'; wire the set onto the edge and deliver the same day again and all of it lands
